name: Hub Group

reads.name: What they do
reads.evidence: Hub Group sells intermodal (container-on-train plus truck) freight moves, dedicated trucking and logistics services in North America; it books the move, buys rail and truck capacity, and keeps the spread. Last audited filing (FY2024 10-K) is now declared unreliable.

reads.name: What they sell
reads.evidence: Two segments: ITS (intermodal and dedicated trucking) about $2.2B and Logistics (final mile, managed transportation, consolidation/fulfilment, brokerage) about $1.6B of roughly $3.7B FY2025 revenue (preliminary, unaudited). FY2024 revenue was $3.95B in the 10-K before restatement.

reads.name: Who buys
reads.evidence: Retail, consumer products, automotive and durables shippers. Top 10 customers were 44% of 2024 revenue; one customer exceeded 10% of revenue in each of 2022-2024.

reads.name: Where they operate
reads.evidence: North America; 2023 purchase of a controlling stake in EASO (Mexico) adds cross-border intermodal. Geographic revenue split and currency exposure not re-checked in a restated filing; peso exposure is small but unquantified here.

reads.name: Money model
reads.evidence: Take-rate/spread model: resells rail and drayage capacity at a markup; revenue is mostly per-load and contract based, not subscription. Two-sentence explanation holds. Margin is thin (2024 operating income $140M on $3.95B, about 3.6%, pre-restatement) and the restatement hit purchased-transportation cost, the core cost line.

reads.name: Operations
reads.evidence: Asset-light-ish: capex $51M in 2024 and about $45M in 2025 against D&A of $193M in 2024 (owns about 50,000 53-foot containers, 2,300 tractors). Costs are mostly purchased transportation (variable) but the company says H1 2026 was an operating loss before one-offs. Guidance hit rate is unreadable: FY2026 revenue outlook cut from $3.65-3.95B (Feb) to $3.6-3.8B (Sep).

reads.name: Supply chain
reads.evidence: Critical inputs: rail line-haul (10-K says it relies on contractual relationships with two railroads; supplier names not stated in the text read, mapper context names Union Pacific/CSX), drayage (about 73% own fleet and owner-operators in 2024), diesel, containers/tractors. Single point of failure is rail access and rate. H1 2026 higher fuel, rail and drayage costs hit results before rate increases began in Q3 2026, so pass-through lags (signal tags: oil/diesel, fuel surcharge lag, rail rates, wages). Tightening truck capacity is helping pricing.

reads.name: Edge
reads.evidence: Scale in marketing intermodal for the railroads (railroads have chosen to rely on marketers like Hub per the 10-K), GPS-tracked container fleet, drayage network. Edge is thin: shippers can switch marketers, and railroads could sell direct. New in 2026: cost-reduction and yield-management programmes and a new CEO.

reads.name: Everyday brand
reads.evidence: Business-to-business freight marketer; consumers would not notice it vanishing. No marketing-spend disclosure read. Name known inside logistics only.

reads.name: Rivals and share
reads.evidence: Competes with J.B. Hunt, Schneider, rail-owned intermodal marketing and other 3PLs. Hub intermodal volume +1% in Q4 2025 and 'relatively stable' in H1 2026 while AAR industry intermodal ran +5.1% YTD to Nov 21 (rail data), which suggests flat-to-lost share (inference).

reads.name: Growth runway
reads.evidence: Truck-to-rail conversion in tightening capacity and Mexico cross-border are real; Q4 2025 Logistics demand was soft and brokerage volume fell 10% with revenue per load down 4%. Nothing scaling unpriced that can be verified.

reads.name: Cash and leaders
reads.evidence: Last reported (preliminary) 2025 operating cash flow about $194M, capex $45M, net debt about $116M at 2025 year-end; but June 30, 2026 net debt about $66M then $75M drawn on the revolver in Aug 2026. Buybacks $68M in 2024 and $14M in 2025. CFO departed May 2026 (interim CFO paid $125k a month), CEO swapped to David Yeager (73) in Sep 2026, and the Yeager family used majority voting control (Class B, about 61.7% of votes) on Oct 1, 2026 to remove 3 directors without cause. Pay is tied to EBITDA as a percent of gross margin, which relies on the same costs that were misstated.

reads.name: Durability
reads.evidence: Intermodal remains relevant, but the company has lost control of its books, its CFO, a stable board and (possibly) its listing. Not a Zoom-type fade; the risk is execution and governance.

reads.name: Red flags
reads.evidence: Two Item 4.02 non-reliance 8-Ks: Feb 5, 2026 (Q1-Q3 2025 misstated; purchased transportation and payables understated, $77M reduction recorded in those periods) and May 11/12, 2026 (audited FY2024 and FY2023 misstated; transactions 'prematurely or incorrectly recognized or not adequately supported'). NT 10-K (Mar 3), NT 10-Q (May 12, Aug 11, Nov 10). Company expects to conclude controls were ineffective for 2023, 2024 and 2025. 10-K for 2025 and three 2026 10-Qs unfiled. Nasdaq: staff delisting determination Sep 16, 2026; panel exception to Dec 31, 2026, hard limit Mar 12, 2027; new Q3 notice Nov 17. Lender deadline moved three times, now Jan 31, 2027.

reads.name: Regime fit
reads.evidence: Boom good (volume, operating leverage), overheat mixed (fuel/rail/drayage costs ran ahead of pricing in H1 2026), stagflation poor, slowdown poor (retail import volumes forecast down; thin margin on a fixed cost base; levered to retail). Sensitive to diesel, rail rates and the dollar via cross-border.

reads.name: Rules and politics
reads.evidence: No specific pending regulatory docket read. Exposure is to rail rate and service regulation indirectly, trucking safety rules and tariffs on imports (volume). Nasdaq delisting process and SEC comment-letter status unknown; no CORRESP/UPLOAD letters found in the filing list since April 2024.

reads.name: Price
reads.evidence: Price $23.28 (2026-11-25 close basis), market cap about $1.42B, 52-week range $22.34 to $53.26, near the 5-year low (5-year close avg $38.87). Reverse DCF on enterprise value about $1.55B (cap plus about $141M net debt using $198M debt less $132M cash plus $75M revolver draw): if FCF base is the preliminary 2025 level of about $149M (OCF 194 less capex 45), price implies about -2% a year; if true FCF is lower, e.g. $100M, it implies about +4%, at $60M about +11%. H1 2026 was an operating loss and no audited FCF exists, so the base cannot be trusted and no cushion can be claimed. P/E and EV/EBITDA vs own history and peers: not computable on unreliable earnings.

status_reason: Kill switch 6.4.1: unresolved accounting red flags (two Item 4.02 non-reliance filings covering 2023-2025, controls ineffective, 10-K and three 10-Qs unfiled, Nasdaq delisting process live to Dec 31, 2026 / Mar 12, 2027 limit).

feedback.fact: Hub says H1 2026 results were hurt by higher fuel, rail and drayage costs before rate increases that began in Q3 2026, while tightening truck capacity supported over-the-road conversion to intermodal. Fits late Overheat cost squeeze plus intermodal strength seen in AAR data.
